**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 4.2/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-06-15, latest 2026-06-15

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; Devyani International Limited will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Devyani described (August 26, 2026) as already 'a company listed on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited'; Sapphire to be dissolved without winding up on effectiveness; exchange observation letters valid six months from June 12, 2026 to file with NCLT

**The stages, as filed:** announced (2026-06-15)

**Stated in the filings:** resulting company **Devyani International Limited**.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Not a separation: all of Sapphire Foods' KFC/Pizza Hut QSR business amalgamated into Devyani International — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* SFML and other Sapphire promoters, including QSR Management Trust, to be reclassified in 'public category' of Devyani; RJ Corp remains Devyani's promoter
- *What it reveals:* Swap 177 Devyani shares per 100 Sapphire; Sapphire net worth INR 13,269.93mn exceeds Devyani's 10,381.02mn on lower revenue (24,510.76mn vs 33,493.33mn), implying asset-heavy, less-levered Sapphire
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Promoters reclassified as public in Devyani; SFML's terminated 18.5% block sale to Arctic may be revived as secondary transaction
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Explanatory statement to shareholders: valuation reports, fairness opinions and share exchange ratio basis; Sapphire assets transferred
- *In their words:* “SFML and the other promoters and members of the promoter group of the Transferor Company will be classified in the ‘public category’ of shareholders of the Transferee Company after the Scheme is effective.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The supplied texts do not contain management's rationale, and none can be reconstructed from them without inventing content. The "CALL PASSAGES" section of the prompt is empty — no earnings call extracts from any year were included — and the material labelled "SCHEME RATIONALE" is not the scheme's rationale section: it is the NSE and BSE observation/No-Objection letters dated June 12, 2026, relaying SEBI's comments on the draft scheme. Those letters only describe the transaction's legal shape and what must later be disclosed; the rationale is listed as a future disclosure obligation ("The rationale and objectives underlying the proposed scheme") rather than stated. What the letters do establish is that this is a composite Scheme of Arrangement under sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 between Sapphire Foods India Limited as Transferor Company and Devyani International Limited as Transferee Company, filed under Regulation 37 of SEBI LODR, with assets and liabilities of Sapphire being transferred to Devyani, a share exchange ratio supported by registered valuer reports and merchant banker fairness opinions, promoter and promoter group entities of Sapphire and Devyani intending reclassification into the Public Category in Devyani, and a linked "SFIL Secondary Sale" of up to 5,94,55,837 equity shares — up to 18.5% of Sapphire's share capital as of December 31, 2025 — by Sapphire Foods Mauritius Limited to Arctic International Limited. The structure described is a transfer/amalgamation of Sapphire into Devyani rather than a separation of a business out of Sapphire, so even the premise of the question (which business is being separated, and why) is not supported by these documents. SEBI also required the scheme to be expressly subject to Competition Commission of India approval before NCLT filing, which is consistent with a combination of two operators rather than a carve-out. No numbers cited by management, no named business line being separated, no problems the separation would solve, and no requesting party (investors, lenders or brand partners) appear anywhere in the provided text.

**How it evolved:** No evolution can be traced: zero earnings call passages were provided, so there are no call dates, no first mention, and no change in plan to report. The only dated item in the material is June 12, 2026 — the date of SEBI's comment letter and of the NSE and BSE observation letters, whose validity runs six months from that date for filing the scheme with NCLT. The only sequencing visible is procedural: draft scheme filed with the exchanges, SEBI comments, exchange NOC, CCI approval, then NCLT petition and shareholder approval.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated. The provided texts contain no management commentary on margins, capital allocation, valuation, focus, or standalone prospects for either entity. SEBI merely requires that such effects — impact on shareholders including dilution or change in rights, a cost-benefit analysis, three years of Revenue, PAT and EBITDA for both companies, and Devyani's post-scheme balance sheet — be disclosed later in the explanatory statement to shareholders.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The filing is a Scheme of Arrangement under sections 230–232 of the Companies Act, 2013 in which Sapphire Foods India Limited is the Transferor Company and Devyani International Limited is the Transferee Company — a combination of the two listed operators, not a carve-out of a business unit from Sapphire. “We refer to your application for Scheme of Arrangement by Sapphire Foods India Limited ("Sapphire"/"Transferor Company") and Devyani International Limited ("Devyani"/"Transferee Company") and their respective shareholders under sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 filed with the Exchange under Regulation 37 of SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015, read with SEBI Master circular no. SEBI/HO/CFD/POD-2/P/CIR/2023/93 dated June 20, 2023.”
- *Scheme* — The rationale itself is absent from this document — SEBI treats it as something the companies must still explain to shareholders in the explanatory statement, alongside a cost-benefit analysis. “b) The rationale and objectives underlying the proposed scheme.”
- *Scheme* — Assets and liabilities move from Sapphire to Devyani, which must be quantified along with Devyani's post-scheme balance sheet — confirming the direction of transfer. “The value of Assets and liabilities of Sapphire being transferred to Devyani and post-scheme balance sheet of Devyani.”
- *Scheme* — A concurrent secondary sale is attached to the scheme: up to 5,94,55,837 Sapphire shares, up to 18.5% of share capital as of December 31, 2025, sold by Sapphire Foods Mauritius Limited to Arctic International Limited; shareholding patterns must be shown both with and without it. “Disclose details of SFIL Secondary Sale i.e. Sale of up to 5,94,55,837 Equity Shares of the Sapphire representing up to 18.5% of the share capital of the Sapphire as of December 31, 2025, by Sapphire Foods Mauritius Limited to Arctic International Limited.”
- *Scheme* — Certain promoter and promoter group entities of both companies intend to be reclassified into the public category in Devyani, implying a change in control composition of the combined entity. “Disclose details of Promoters and Promoter Group entities of Sapphire and Devyani intending to be reclassified in the Public Category in Devyani, and the reasons thereof.”
- *Scheme* — SEBI conditioned the scheme on Competition Commission of India approval before any NCLT filing, and on share exchange ratio support from registered valuers and merchant bankers. “The entities are advised to ensure that the captioned Scheme of Arrangement is made expressly subject to receipt of approval from the Competition Commission of India (CCI), as applicable; and that the company shall not file the Scheme before the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) unless and until the requisite approval from CCI is obtained.”
- *Scheme* — NSE conveyed No Objection under Regulation 37, valid six months from June 12, 2026, while disclaiming any view on the scheme's financial soundness or the correctness of statements made. “The validity of this "Observation Letter" shall be six months from June 12, 2026, within which the Scheme shall be submitted to NCLT.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything substantive: no earnings call passages were supplied, and the scheme text given is only the exchanges' observation letters. No stated rationale, business identified, numbers, requesting party, or timeline.

- *In their words:* “The proposed IPO remains subject to receipt of applicable approvals, prevailing market conditions, and other relevant considerations.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

These texts do not contain a stated rationale for separating a business, and no scheme of arrangement/demerger rationale section is present — the document labelled "Scheme Rationale" is in fact two SEBI LODR Regulation 30 disclosures by Coal India Ltd., neither of which gives reasons. The first (Ref. CIL:XI(D):4157/4156:2026:35185, dated 02.09.2026) discloses that the draft red herring prospectus dated 1st September 2026 of Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL), a wholly owned subsidiary of CIL, was filed with SEBI, BSE and NSE, for a proposed IPO structured purely as an Offer for Sale of up to 661,836,300 equity shares of face value INR 2 each held by Coal India Limited — i.e. a partial monetisation/listing of a producing coal subsidiary by the parent, not a demerger, and explicitly "subject to receipt of applicable approvals, prevailing market conditions, and other relevant considerations." No objects-of-the-issue, value-unlocking, focus, margin or capital-allocation reasoning is given, and no investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for it. The second (Ref. CIL:XID:04156/157:35043, dated 27.07.2026) is the opposite of a separation: CIL's Board approved investing in the rights issue of CIL Rajasthan Akshay Urja Limited (CRAUL), a renewable-energy JV with Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Urja Nigam Limited (RVUNL) incorporated 09.06.2025, with CIL subscribing 2,22,000 shares at Rs. 10 each (Rs. 22,20,000) and RVUNL 78,000 shares (Rs. 7,80,000), holding 74%/26%; paid-up capital Rs. 10,00,000 and size/turnover NIL, to develop solar, PSP and wind projects selling power to RVUNL under Section 62 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and to DISCOMs/third parties/C&I customers. The only call passage supplied (Feb 2024) runs directly against a separation thesis: asked whether renewables/alternative energy would be held as a separate demerged entity, management said the verticals already sit in existing subsidiaries and joint ventures, that no new subsidiary would be created, and that it "is not in our discussion right now"; the only numbers-adjacent remarks are that coal mine capex will be met from internal accruals, with little debt in FY25 but rising debt in the following year for renewal and gasification projects. On this evidence the correct answer is that CIL is not documented here as separating a business — it is listing a minority stake in MCL by Offer for Sale while continuing to fund renewables inside CIL's own subsidiary/JV structure.

**How it evolved:** Feb 2024 call: an investor (Venkatesh Subramanian) raised the idea unprompted, asking whether renewables/alternative energy would be carved out as a separate demerged entity; management rejected it, saying subsidiaries and JVs already exist, no new subsidiary would be created, and it was not under discussion. No 2025 or later call passages were provided, so there is no call-by-call progression toward a separation. The only later developments in these texts are corporate actions without commentary: the 27.07.2026 CRAUL rights-issue investment (keeping renewables in-house) and the 02.09.2026 disclosure of MCL's DRHP for an Offer-for-Sale IPO of CIL-held shares.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated. Management gave no expected effect on margins, capital, valuation or focus for any entity; in Feb 2024 they said existing subsidiaries and JVs already serve the purpose and no separation was under discussion. The MCL DRHP disclosure gives only deal mechanics — an Offer for Sale of CIL-held shares, so no primary proceeds to MCL — with no articulated benefit.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Feb 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06da4b0a-5420-4ecc-aa42-737719710147.pdf)* — The separation idea came from an investor, not management — Venkatesh Subramanian asked whether the alternative/renewable energy business, alongside coal and CIL energy, would eventually be held as a separate demerged entity. “And do you have any plans going forward once we have coal, we have CIL energy and then we have -- we're investing a lot in terms of alternative energy as well. Would you have that as a separate demerged entity or something in the future?”
- *[Feb 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06da4b0a-5420-4ecc-aa42-737719710147.pdf)* — Management declined the demerger idea, saying renewable and other non-coal verticals are already housed in existing subsidiaries and joint ventures and that no new subsidiary was planned. “We had already -- some verticals are there for the renewable energy and other projects, for that we had already subsidiaries companies are there.”
- *[Feb 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06da4b0a-5420-4ecc-aa42-737719710147.pdf)* — Management stated explicitly that a separate demerged entity was not on the agenda at that time. “We are not going to create any new subsidy. It is not in our discussion right now.”
- *[Feb 2024](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=06da4b0a-5420-4ecc-aa42-737719710147.pdf)* — On funding, management confirmed coal mine capex would come from internal accruals with minimal debt in FY25, but flagged rising debt from the following year for mine renewal and coal gasification projects — the only capital-structure specifics given. “Yes, you are right because we had just started the renewal, so not much debt will come in the '25. But in the coming year, debt will increase in the renewal and gasification projects.”
- *Scheme* — The filing dated 02.09.2026 is a Regulation 30 disclosure, not a scheme of arrangement: it reports that MCL's DRHP dated 1 September 2026 was filed with SEBI, BSE and NSE for an IPO that is entirely an Offer for Sale of up to 661,836,300 shares of INR 2 face value held by CIL, with no rationale, objects of the issue or value-unlocking argument stated. “The DRHP filing pertains to the proposed Initial Public Offering (“IPO”) of MCL, comprising an Offer for Sale of up to 661,836,300 equity shares having a face value of INR 2 each, held by Coal India Limited.”
- *Scheme* — The IPO is conditional and unscheduled in these texts, dependent on approvals and market conditions. “The proposed IPO remains subject to receipt of applicable approvals, prevailing market conditions, and other relevant considerations.”
- *Scheme* — The second disclosure (27.07.2026) shows renewables being funded inside the group rather than separated: CIL's Board approved participating in CRAUL's rights issue, subscribing 2,22,000 shares at Rs. 10 each (Rs. 22,20,000) versus RVUNL's 78,000 shares (Rs. 7,80,000), retaining the 74:26 split in an entity with Rs. 10,00,000 paid-up capital and NIL turnover, incorporated 09.06.2025. “CIL Board at its meeting held on date has inter -alia, accorded approval for investment in Right s Issue of CIL Rajasthan Akshay Urja Limited ( CRAUL ) by Coal India Limited , details as per Annexure.”
- *Scheme* — CRAUL's stated business purpose is solar, pumped-storage and wind generation with power sold to RVUNL under Section 62 of the Electricity Act, 2003, or to DISCOMs, third parties, the open market and C&I customers anywhere in India. “To develop, construct and operate the solar power projects, PSP projects and wind power projects or such other projects as may be mutually agreed between the Parties in writing through a suitable model, and the Company will undertake the business of sellin g the power generated from the Projects to RVUNL under Section 62 of Electricity Act, 2003 or such other entities as may be mutually agreed between Parties in accordance with the applicable Laws”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything substantive: no scheme rationale, no MCL financials, valuation, use of proceeds or OFS reasoning, no investor/lender/partner demand, no post-listing control or capital-allocation plan, and no 2025–2026 call commentary.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 3.6/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 1 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-01-29, latest 2026-01-29

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2026-01-29)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** The FMCG / consumer products business, RCPL, separated out of the retail business — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* The FMCG arm carries over 5,000 Crores of turnover, up 60% year-on-year, and is being pulled out of retail; retail loses a month of that revenue in Q3 and more, plus margin, from the next quarter.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents state no size, shareholding, index status or listing detail for the demerged entity.
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The RCPL demerger scheme of arrangement, and Q4 retail revenue and margin ex-RCPL
- *In their words:* “On the FMCG side, the demerger happened on 1st December.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The business being separated is Reliance's FMCG arm, Reliance Consumer Products Ltd. (RCPL) — the Campa-led packaged consumer goods business — which was demerged out of Reliance Retail (Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd., RRVL) into a direct subsidiary of Reliance Industries Ltd., effective 1 December 2025. On the Jul 2025 call management framed it as a business that had outgrown its host: it had "built an own independent distribution network, which is pretty substantial," had run a high-decibel IPL campaign for Campa with "very high recall," and had reached "double digit market share in key markets," while rapidly expanding supply chain and building world-class manufacturing and R&D with automation and backward integration to deliver product superiority and the lowest cost. Management said retail and FMCG already dealt with each other at arm's length even inside the group, so the demerger simply converts that into full legal independence — "these two become completely independent" — rather than changing commercial terms. Structurally it was presented as neutral for owners: RCPL was a 100% subsidiary of RRVL and "will just move out and shareholding will get replicated," i.e. the same RRVL shareholders hold the FMCG entity directly, with completion gated only on regulatory approvals (still pending as of Jul 2025). The numbers cited to justify standalone scale came in Jan 2026: FMCG turnover of more than Rs.5,000 Crores, up 60% year-on-year, built partly on purchased brands. The flip side management quantified is accounting, not strategic: RCPL's revenue leaving Reliance Retail depressed reported retail growth (Jan 2026 reported +8.1% with RCPL in for only part of the quarter; Apr 2026 reported +11% versus almost 14% adjusted; Jul 2026 reported +7.4% versus 11.6% underlying), and management repeatedly asked analysts to read retail growth ex-RCPL. Notably, no investor, lender or partner was named as having requested the separation — in these passages the demerger is management-initiated, and analysts (CLSA, Investec) only probed its timing and its drag on reported retail numbers.

**How it evolved:** On the Jul 2025 call the demerger was disclosed as in flight — the FMCG business was "in the process of being demerged out of Reliance Retail into a subsidiary of Reliance Industries," with Dinesh Taluja telling CLSA's Vikash Jain it was "not yet" done and "under regulatory approvals," and Anshuman Thakur confirming the 100% RRVL subsidiary would move out with shareholding replicated. By the Jan 2026 call it was completed effective 1 December 2025, with FMCG turnover disclosed at over Rs.5,000 Crores (+60% YoY) and the first partial-quarter accounting impact on Reliance Retail explained; Investec's Harit Kapoor pressed on the like-to-like and margin effect from the next quarter. In Apr 2026 and Jul 2026 the discussion had narrowed entirely to adjusting reported retail growth for the lost RCPL revenue (almost 14% vs 11% reported in Q4; 11.6% underlying vs 7.4% reported in Q1 FY27), with no further strategic rationale added.

**What management expects from it:** For FMCG/RCPL: a completely independent business with its own distribution, world-class low-cost manufacturing and R&D, double-digit share in key markets and turnover above Rs.5,000 Crores growing 60%, held directly under RIL with replicated shareholding. For Reliance Retail: no stated benefit — only a mechanical loss of RCPL revenue, with growth to be read adjusted (14% vs 11%, 11.6% vs 7.4%).

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Jul 2025* — Management disclosed that the FMCG (Campa-led consumer products) business was mid-demerger out of Reliance Retail into a direct subsidiary of Reliance Industries, to become an independent business once regulatory approvals were in place. “It is in the process of being demerged out of Reliance Retail into a subsidiary of Reliance Industries.”
- *Jul 2025* — The separation was justified on standalone operating capability: an independent distribution network, double-digit market share in key markets after the high-decibel IPL Campa campaign, and world-class manufacturing/R&D with automation and backward integration for product superiority and lowest cost. “We did a very high decibel campaign during IP L for Campa, which has a very high recall. And we now have double digit market share in key markets.”
- *Jul 2025* — Management argued the demerger changes legal status, not commercial dealing, because retail and FMCG already transacted at arm's length inside the group — the two now become fully independent. “And we have, even today we have an arm's length relationship between our retail business and our FMCG business, but then these two become completely independent.”
- *Jul 2025* — In Q&A with Vikash Jain (CLSA), management confirmed the demerger was not complete and was awaiting regulatory approvals before the business would move out. “Not yet, it is under regulatory approvals.”
- *Jul 2025* — Anshuman Thakur described the mechanics as ownership-neutral: a 100% RRVL subsidiary moving out with the identical shareholder base replicated at the demerged entity. “Today it is 100% sub of RR VL, it will just move out and shareholding will get replicated.”
- *Jan 2026* — The demerger was completed effective 1 December 2025, and management cited FMCG scale of over Rs.5,000 Crores turnover, up 60% year-on-year, aided by brand purchases. “On the FMCG side, the demerger happened on 1st December. And we are at more than 5,000 Crores of turnover, and this is 60% up on a year -on-year basis.”
- *Jan 2026* — Dinesh Taluja named the RCPL demerger as one of three factors distorting Reliance Retail's reported revenue (Rs.97,600 Crores, +8.1%), since RCPL's revenue was fully in Q2 and then exited the retail business. “And then the third part is the RCPL demerger, which was effective during the quarter. So RCPL's entire revenue was included in Q2.”
- *Jan 2026* — Harit Kapoor (Investec) pushed management for the like-to-like retail growth and the margin impact once the demerger affects a full quarter, estimating roughly a 1% revenue impact; Taluja confirmed only one month of revenue had exited so far. “This is the first quarter where there is an RCPL demerger and from the next quarter it will be entirely there , so if you could just give us a sense of ex the merger what the like -to-like growth would be for the retail business”
- *Apr 2026* — With retail revenue at a record Rs.98,000 Crores (+11%), management directed investors to the ex-RCPL view: almost 14% growth for the quarter adjusted for the demerger and 12% for the full year, even higher excluding RCPL. “Now, if you recollect, RCPL business was demerged out in the last quarter adjusted for that, the growth is almost 14%, for the full year the growth is 12% and if you exclude RCP L demerger the growth would be even higher.”
- *Jul 2026* — A full-quarter demerger effect opened a wide gap between reported and underlying retail growth, with EBITDA margin at 7.9% (down 80 bps YoY) attributed to digital/dark-store investment rather than the demerger. “Adjusted for that, the underlying revenue growth is 11.6%. On a reported basis, the growth is 7.4%.”
- *Scheme* — The filing text supplied as the scheme rationale contains no RCPL demerger rationale at all — it is a set of unrelated Regulation 30 disclosures (SevenHills Healthcare resolution plan approval, the STPL–Jiostar merger effective 30 November 2025, and the Radisys Cayman–Radisys International merger). “This is further to our disclosure dated November 14, 2024,  wherein we had intimated about the scheme of arrangement for merger of Star Television Productions Limited (“ STPL ”), a subsidiary of the Company  with Star India Private Limited ( now known as Jiostar India Private Limited) (“ Jiostar ”), another subsidiary of the Company .”

*Not explained on the calls:* No stated valuation, listing, capital-allocation or tax logic; no RCPL standalone EBITDA/margins; no investor, lender or partner demand; supplied scheme text has no rationale.

## TMPV — Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 3.6/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 4 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-10-09, latest 2025-11-10

> **Listing:** LISTED — the resulting company trades since about 2025-10-15

**The stages, as filed:** listed (2025-10-15)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Commercial Vehicles business undertaking of Tata Motors Limited, demerged into TMLCV, later renamed Tata Motors Limited — class `not stated`.

- *Insiders:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* Demerger accounting recorded a profit of ~Rs. 83,000 Cr on disposal of the CV undertaking, being fair value of CV assets; continuing TMPV retains passenger vehicles plus investments in the Electric Vehicle business and JLR, with net debt ~Rs. 30,000 Cr at March 2026.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — 1:1 shares allotted to all 3,68,23,31,373 TML holders; untradeable Oct 15–Nov 12; record-date price discovery mechanism.
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* TMLCV/Tata Motors Limited information memorandum and the Rs. 83,000 Cr disposal profit and debt allocation in TMPV's accounts
- *In their words:* “In terms of the Scheme, the Commercial Vehicles business undertaking of TML has been demerged into TMLCV and TMPV stands amalgamated with TML.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Across these texts the separation is a composite scheme of arrangement under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act that splits erstwhile Tata Motors Limited into two listed entities: the Commercial Vehicles business undertaking is demerged into TML Commercial Vehicles Limited (renamed Tata Motors Limited), while the existing listed company is renamed Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited and carries the passenger vehicles business together with its investments in the Electric Vehicle business and JLR. The only explicit structural reason management gave on the calls is a holding-company problem: the PV business, which sat as a subsidiary (TML) of the listed company, had to be merged upward into the listed parent 'because you don't want the top Company to be construed as a CIC and hence this becomes a proper operating company' (Aug 2024) — i.e. so the PV-side listed entity is an operating company rather than a core investment company. The second stated benefit is disclosure and accountability per business: on May 2024 Balaji said the CV business had just delivered its highest-ever revenue of Rs. 78,800 Cr with double-digit EBITDA (Q4 ~12%), PBT(bei) of almost Rs. 6,000 Cr and about $1 billion of EBITDA, and added that 'as we demerge this business, you will start hearing more and more granular details about this as we go forward.' The economics management quantified were mechanical: a 1:1 share entitlement, an asset split as on the appointed date of broadly 60:40 CV:PV (the 40% being investments at book value in the PV company, EV company and JLR, India standalone only, excluding JLR's own operations), and tax-neutrality for both the CV and PV undertakings and for shareholders. The backdrop was a company deleveraging into strength — FY24 consolidated revenue up ~27% to Rs. 4.4 lakh Cr with EBITDA of 14.3%, EBIT 8.3% and PBT(bei) of almost Rs. 29,000 Cr, JLR repaying over GBP 1.8 billion of debt, and by Feb 2025 net automotive debt of Rs. 19,000 Cr with the domestic Indian business back to net cash of Rs. 700 Cr — so the separation was not presented as a rescue of a weak arm. Valuation of the separated arm was only revealed after the fact: in Nov 2025 TMPV disclosed the CV undertaking was valued at ~Rs. 94,000 Cr by third-party agencies against ~Rs. 11,000 Cr of book value transferred, producing a notional Rs. 83,000 Cr disposal profit fully offset by a contra deemed dividend, with no impact on distributable reserves or net worth. Costs were acknowledged only in May 2026, where stamp duty charges for the demerger sat inside ~Rs. 4,100 Cr of FY26 exceptionals. Notably, in none of these passages does management articulate a strategic 'why' — no claim of unlocking value, sharpening capital allocation, differing cycles or investor demand — and the attached filing text is purely procedural.

**How it evolved:** By the May 10, 2024 call the scheme already existed in principle and management was 'working at frenetic pace to bring the scheme to the Board for approval', alongside the DVR cancellation EGM that carried >99.5% majority-of-minority approval. The Aug 2024 call is where the mechanics were spelled out: a two-step transaction (CV undertaking out into a new CV ListCo, then the PV subsidiary merged up into the existing listed company to avoid CIC classification), 1:1 entitlement, ~60:40 asset split, tax-neutral, 12-15 months, appointed date targeted at July 1, 2025, with RBI, stock exchange, SEBI and NCLT approvals in train and all corporate actions to be closed before the demerger. Execution then tracked almost exactly to that calendar — Feb 2025 awaiting SEBI/exchange NOCs and first flagging an effective date 'more like October this year'; May 13, 2025 reporting 'overwhelming votes in our favor' and confirming July 1 appointed / Oct 1, 2025 effective; Aug 8, 2025 with the NCLT final hearing concluded and judgment reserved. The Scheme became effective October 1, 2025 (record date Oct 14, CV shares listed Nov 12), after which the Nov 14, 2025 call was TMPV's first results as a listed entity under a new CFO voice (Dhiman Gupta), with Feb 2026 and May 14, 2026 showing the post-split entity reporting only JLR plus Tata PV, its own Rs. 3 dividend and its own Rs. 30,000 Cr net debt.

**What management expects from it:** Explicitly only three things: more granular per-business disclosure once CV is demerged (May 2024); a PV-side listed entity that is a proper operating company rather than a CIC (Aug 2024); and two separately listed companies with 1:1 shareholding, a ~60:40 asset split and tax neutrality. TMPV retains PV, EV and JLR investments. No per-entity margin, capital-allocation or valuation targets were given in these texts.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *May 2024* — The scheme was already in motion and being rushed to the Board; the DVR cancellation had just cleared with >99.5% majority-of-minority approval, signalling shareholder receptivity to the corporate-action programme. “And of course, on the demerger, we are working at frenetic pace to bring the scheme to the Board for approval.”
- *May 2024* — Management framed better per-business disclosure as a direct consequence of separating the CV arm, which had just posted Rs. 78,800 Cr revenue, ~12% Q4 EBITDA, PBT(bei) of almost Rs. 6,000 Cr and ~$1 billion of EBITDA. “And as we demerge this business, you will start hearing more and more granular details about this as we go forward.”
- *Aug 2024* — The only explicit structural rationale given anywhere in these texts: the PV subsidiary is merged up into the listed parent so the top listed company is not treated as a core investment company but as a genuine operating company. “That is important to get done because you don't want the top Company to be construed as a CIC and hence this becomes a proper operating company.”
- *Aug 2024* — The two-step mechanics and naming: CV undertaking carved out into a new CV ListCo which takes the renamed 'TML', while the existing listed company becomes Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and absorbs everything left behind. “Along with that, the CV Company, the newly formed CV Company will be renamed as TML and the existing TML Company will be renamed as Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles.”
- *Aug 2024* — The economic terms: 1:1 entitlement for every Tata Motors shareholder on the record date, a broadly 60:40 CV:PV asset split at the appointed date, and tax neutrality for both undertakings and for shareholders. “One of the most important number is the asset ratio as on the appointed date, we expect it to be broadly 60:40, that is 60% as CV 40% as the residual PV that will be there.”
- *Aug 2024* — In answer to Jinesh Gandhi, Balaji clarified the 60:40 is India standalone only, and the residual 40% is book-value investments in the PV company, EV company and JLR — not JLR's operating value. “So for whatever is remaining is the 40%, they are basically investments that company holds into the PV company, EV company JLR. It is the investment value which is all at book value.”
- *Aug 2024* — All other corporate actions — RBI approval, stock exchange approvals, DVR cancellation and issue of ordinary shares — were sequenced deliberately to close before the demerger. “So all the corporate actions are running at full speed and we intend to get all of them closed before the demerger.”
- *Feb 2025* — Regulatory progress on track with SEBI/exchange NOCs imminent; the timetable firms up to a July 1 appointed date with an October effective date, against net automotive debt of Rs. 19,000 Cr and the domestic business back to net cash of Rs. 700 Cr. “And, therefore, we are expecting to have the appointed date as July 1st. If all goes well in terms of just dates from the honorable NCLT and effective date is likely to be more like October this year.”
- *Jun 2025* — Shareholder vote carried decisively and the final calendar is locked in; the same call confirmed the Tata Capital stake would travel with the CV business. “The demerger update: we had overwhelming votes in our favor and therefore we are on track for an appointed date of July 1st and an effective date of October 1st 2025.”
- *Aug 2025* — The last approval hurdle cleared in substance — NCLT final hearing concluded with judgment reserved — keeping the 1 October effective date intact alongside the Iveco acquisition and a Moody's upgrade of JLR to Ba1. “We had the NCLT final hearing today and it has been concluded and the judgment is reserved. And that should help us complete this quarter. And the effective date for the demerger will be 1st October, on plan.”
- *Scheme* — The filing states the legal outcome: the CV business undertaking is demerged into TMLCV and TMPV is amalgamated with TML, effective October 1, 2025 with an appointed date of July 1, 2025, sanctioned by NCLT Mumbai on August 25 and September 10, 2025. “In terms of the Scheme, the Commercial Vehicles business undertaking of TML has been demerged into TMLCV and TMPV stands amalgamated with TML.”
- *Scheme* — The surviving listed entity keeps the PV business plus the EV and JLR investments under the new TMPV name, with the CV company taking the Tata Motors Limited name; price discovery on the record date adjusts the TML share price. “Pursuant to the Scheme, Tata Motors Limited shall change its name to Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited and shall carry on the passenger vehicles business including its investments in Electric Vehicle business and JLR.”

*Not explained on the calls:* No stated strategic why — no value-unlock, capital-allocation, cycle-divergence or focus argument; no investor, lender or partner demand named; no separation cost quantified ex ante.

*Calls read (36 months):* Aug 2024, Aug 2025, Feb 2025, Feb 2026, Jun 2025, Jun 2026, May 2024, Nov 2025

## ADANIENT — Adani Enterprises Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **LISTED <1Y — selling-pressure window; the bargain forms here** · score 2.9/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 4 filing(s) from NSE · first 2025-11-26, latest 2026-04-01

> **Listing:** LISTED — the resulting company trades since about 2026-04-01

**The stages, as filed:** nclt_sanction (2025-11-26) → effective (2026-04-01) → listed (2026-04-01)

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Core infrastructure and services platforms — Airports, Roads, ANIL ecosystem and long-term contracted MDOs — class `value_unlocking`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters of the Company are Gautam S. Adani and Rajesh S. Adani; Gautam S. Adani is Executive Chairman. Stake or incentives in any demerged entity not stated.
- *What it reveals:* 80% of EBITDA share now comes from core infrastructure and services businesses; primary capex phase reaching maturity across businesses, so mature scalable platforms sit inside a holding-company-style parent awaiting unlock.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — not stated
- *Parent or spin:* unclear · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The scheme of arrangement / board approval document for the Airports demerger, with entity-wise EBITDA split
- *In their words:* “AEL is now getting ready for value unlock through demergers.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

Management frames the separation as the final phase of AEL's incubator playbook: AEL builds, stabilizes and scales businesses and then separates them so each can be valued and funded on its own. In the Aug 2024 call the Board had already approved the first such step — the demerger of the Food FMCG business of Adani Enterprises into Adani Wilmar together with its strategic investments in Adani Commodities LLP — on the stated ground that Food FMCG 'has become self-sustained, performing well and poised for future growth', i.e. it no longer needs the incubator and separating it 'unlocks value for shareholders'. By Apr 2026 the same logic is applied to the infrastructure core: AEL closed FY26 with 80% of EBITDA share from core infrastructure and services businesses, its EBITDA profile 'once again transformed into an Infra-Utility portfolio-style', and management said AEL 'is now getting ready for value unlock through demergers' of Airports, Roads, the ANIL (new energy) ecosystem and long-term contracted MDO/mining services — described as independent, sector-leading, large core infra platforms that are 'ready to turn into value creation mode'. The problem the separation solves, as they put it, is that the initial and primary capex phase is reaching maturity across these businesses and the EBITDA mix has shifted to mature, scalable platforms, so holding them inside an incubator no longer reflects their standalone profile; supporting specifics cited were ANIL expanding capacity by 2.5x, solar module domestic sales up 96% YoY, completion of India's largest greenfield Ganga Expressway in under 3.5 years with a 27-year concession, and (Aug 2024) 730 lane km of road built in the quarter with 3 of 10 under-construction projects over 80% complete. Timing is sequenced by business readiness rather than a fixed date: asked specifically about the Airports demerger, Robbie Singh said airport management is 'comfortable around, say, '27, '28'. Separately, the attached scheme filing text covers a different Adani transaction — a composite scheme amalgamating companies under Adani Green Technology Ltd. to consolidate the green hydrogen ecosystem (solar/wind supply-chain manufacturing, green hydrogen generation, downstream products) under one entity — justified by consolidation of resources, operational and administrative efficiencies, economies of scale, lower overheads, fewer duplicated legal and regulatory compliances, expanded business pre-qualifications and capacity for larger/more complex projects, better access to growth funding, combined management skills, a simpler corporate structure, reduced dependency on external factors across the supply chain and cost optimization. No passage here states that investors, lenders or partners requested any of the separations; the only outside prompting visible is a sell-side analyst (Prateek Kumar) pressing on Airports demerger timing.

**How it evolved:** Aug 2024: the idea surfaces as a concrete first step — the Board approves demerging Food FMCG into Adani Wilmar along with the Adani Commodities LLP strategic investments, justified by that business having become self-sustained, and framed inside AEL's incubation track record. By the Apr 2026 call (quarter and year ended March 31, 2026) it has widened from one consumer business into a programme of demergers across the infrastructure core — Airports, Roads, ANIL and contracted MDO — with management stating 80% of FY26 EBITDA now comes from core infrastructure and services and that AEL is 'getting ready for value unlock through demergers'. In the same Apr 2026 Q&A the plan is explicitly sequenced rather than dated: Airports is deferred to management readiness 'around, say, '27, '28', and Copper is still pre-separation, only crossing the revenue threshold for segment disclosure and to be reported as a separate line item from the next quarter.

**What management expects from it:** AEL retains the incubator role, recycling capital into new businesses (Copper next) while separated platforms — Airports, Roads, ANIL, MDO — become independent, sector-leading entities valued on their own mature, contracted, cash-generating EBITDA rather than inside a conglomerate; Food FMCG grows self-sustained inside Adani Wilmar. The green hydrogen scheme expects scale economies, lower overheads, bigger pre-qualifications, cheaper growth funding and cost optimization.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Aug 2024* — The Board approved the first separation — demerging AEL's Food FMCG business into Adani Wilmar, together with AEL's strategic investments in Adani Commodities LLP. “In line with this, the Board of D irectors of Adani Enterprises have approved the demerger of F ood FMCG business o f Adani Enterprise s to Adani Wilm ar, along with its strategic investments in Adani Commodities LLP .”
- *Aug 2024* — The stated test for separating a business is that it has outgrown incubation — Food FMCG was self-sustaining and growing on its own. “The Food FMCG business has become self-sustained , performing well and poised for future growth.”
- *Aug 2024* — The separation is positioned as a continuation of AEL's incubation record of creating sector-leading listed companies and shareholder returns. “Over the years , we have a track record of successfully incubating businesses which are currently leading companies in their respective sectors and delivering substantial returns to their shareholders.”
- *Aug 2024* — Operating evidence cited for the maturing infra businesses: record quarterly road construction and schedule-compliant Ganga Expressway progress. “arter, we have constructed 730 lane kilometer roads, which is the highest for any quarter since its inception.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.adanienterprises.com/-/media/Project/Enterprises/Investors/Investor-Downloads/Results-Conference-Call-Transcripts/Q4-FY26-AEL_Earnings-Call_Transcript.pdf)* — The portfolio mix has shifted decisively to infrastructure — 80% of FY26 EBITDA share from core infrastructure and services — which management uses as the precondition for demerging. “AEL's EBITDA profile has once again transformed into an Infra-Utility portfolio -style as we close this financial year with 80% of the EBITDA share coming from core infrastructure and services businesses.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.adanienterprises.com/-/media/Project/Enterprises/Investors/Investor-Downloads/Results-Conference-Call-Transcripts/Q4-FY26-AEL_Earnings-Call_Transcript.pdf)* — AEL states outright that it is preparing value unlock through demergers. “AEL is now getting ready for value unlock through demergers.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.adanienterprises.com/-/media/Project/Enterprises/Investors/Investor-Downloads/Results-Conference-Call-Transcripts/Q4-FY26-AEL_Earnings-Call_Transcript.pdf)* — The businesses named for separation are Airports, Roads, the ANIL new-energy ecosystem and long-term contracted MDO services, each described as independent and sector-leading. “These businesses are independent, sector -leading , large core infra platform , spread across Airports, Roads, ANIL ecosystem and long -term contract ed MDO services, which are ready to turn into value creation mode.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.adanienterprises.com/-/media/Project/Enterprises/Investors/Investor-Downloads/Results-Conference-Call-Transcripts/Q4-FY26-AEL_Earnings-Call_Transcript.pdf)* — Separation is the fourth and final step of an explicit repeatable incubation sequence, with the first three already completed. “Incubation journey is a repeatable playbook for us: build, stabilize, scale and unlock.”
- *[Apr 2026](https://www.adanienterprises.com/-/media/Project/Enterprises/Investors/Investor-Downloads/Results-Conference-Call-Transcripts/Q4-FY26-AEL_Earnings-Call_Transcript.pdf)* — The trigger is capex maturity: the heavy build phase is ending and EBITDA now comes from mature, scalable platforms, so value unlock is the next step. “So what I want to highlight here is that when you take a broader view of an incubator entity like AEL, what emerges is a clear picture where initial and primary capex phase is reaching maturity across businesses and EBITDA mix has shifted to mature scalable platforms and path for value unlock i s taking shape.”

## HAPPSTMNDS — Happiest Minds Technologies Ltd.

**PROBABLE** (a scheme of arrangement whose nature the documents on file do not settle) · **PRE-SPIN — study the parent; the pieces do not trade yet** · score 2.9/10 · scheme (nature unclear) · 2 filing(s) from NSE · first 2026-06-05, latest 2026-08-18

> **Listing:** NOT YET — scheme at 'announced' stage; the resulting company will list only after NCLT sanction, effectiveness and a record date; indicated timeline: Said August 31, 2026: 'upon the Scheme becoming effective, the shares of the Transferee Company shall be listed and admitted for trading on BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited'; companies 'expect the transaction to be completed over the next 15 months'.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Nothing is spun off; all of Happiest Minds is amalgamated by absorption into ITC Infotech India Limited — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* Promoters held 44.21% (6,73,23,400 shares); Ashok Soota and Ashok Soota Medical Research LLP sell 22.106% at INR 390 then INR 400/share, with non-compete and non-solicitation; ITC Limited becomes promoter with ~73.4%.
- *What it reveals:* Promoter exit at INR 390/400 (avg ~INR 395) prices the equity; the 25:81 swap hands holders ITC Infotech, whose June 30, 2026 turnover INR 1,31,682 lakh and net worth INR 2,31,567 lakh exceed Happiest Minds' INR 62,851 lakh and INR 1,77,550 lakh.
- *Selling pressure:* likely — Happiest Minds will be dissolved and delisted; holders get newly listed ITC Infotech shares in an odd 25:81 ratio, forcing index exclusion.
- *Parent or spin:* spin · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* The draft Scheme and the PwC / GT Valuation Advisors valuation report dated August 31, 2026 on the company's investor page.
- *In their words:* “ITC Limited  will be the promoter  of the merged company,  with a ~73.4 % stake .”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The documents do not describe a separation: the only corporate action in these texts is the opposite — an amalgamation in which Happiest Minds Technologies Ltd (Transferor) is absorbed into ITC Infotech India Ltd (Transferee) and then dissolved without being wound up, under definitive agreements and a Merger Framework Agreement dated August 31, 2026 among Happiest Minds, ITC Infotech, Mr Ashok Soota and Ashok Soota Medical Research LLP. Management's stated reasoning is complementarity and scale: Happiest Minds' AI, digital engineering, cloud, data, analytics and cybersecurity capabilities combined with ITC Infotech's enterprise transformation, SAP, PLM, cloud, Industry 4.0 and industry-specific solutions, to create 'a scaled, AI First Global Technology Services Enterprise' targeting US$1 billion of annual revenue by FY28, with 19,000+ employees, 800+ customers and operations in 30+ countries. The scheme rationale lists: a single globally credible platform from combined capabilities, customer relationships and talent pools; greater synergies via shared financial, managerial, technical and marketing resources; increased scale, focus, cross-selling to a larger customer base, productivity and operational efficiencies, stronger partner-ecosystem relationships and augmented intellectual capital; wider professional opportunities and better employee retention; and an enhanced competitive position in domestic and global markets. Two explicitly financial motives are named: greater efficiency in cash management with 'unfettered access' to combined cash flows for funding growth, and augmentation of the Transferee's ability to raise equity and debt capital. Consideration is share-based — 25 ITC Infotech shares of INR 10 each for every 81 Happiest Minds shares of INR 2 each (other than those held by ITC Infotech itself), based on a joint valuation report of August 31, 2026 by PwC Business Consulting Services LLP and GT Valuation Advisors, with a fairness opinion of the same date from ICICI Securities; ITC Infotech's shares are to be listed by virtue of the scheme, and ITC Infotech separately acquires an aggregate minority stake (amount truncated in the text supplied). Happiest Minds' pre-scheme shareholding as on August 31, 2026 was 6,73,23,400 promoter shares (44.21%) and 8,49,51,411 non-promoter shares (55.79%) of 15,22,74,811 total. The only 'carve-out' discussed on the calls is a measurement exercise, not a business separation: management said AI is spread across the company rather than sitting inside the GBS bucket, so they would go project by project across the whole revenue stream and carve out AI-led revenue — not by technology but by the impact or relevance of AI — to disclose what portion of the quarter's INR 625 crores is AI-led, with the exercise to be completed by end-September and reported at the end of Q2. The texts name no investor, lender or partner as having asked for the transaction.

**How it evolved:** Only one call passage is supplied (Jul 2026), and it contains no reference to any merger, demerger or separation of a business — it addresses only how AI-led revenue will be identified and reported, citing SecAIGenie in security as AI work sitting outside GBS, and committing to a carved-out AI-led revenue number by end-September/end-Q2. The corporate action appears for the first time in the August 31, 2026 filings: the press release announcing the ITC Infotech combination, the Merger Framework Agreement of the same date, and the scheme rationale. So on this evidence the idea cannot be traced call by call; there is no three-year arc in the passages given, and no earlier-call foreshadowing to compare against the final structure.

**What management expects from it:** Not a separation, so no per-entity outcomes are given; Happiest Minds is dissolved into ITC Infotech. The combined entity is expected to gain scale, focus, cross-selling across a larger customer base, productivity and operational efficiencies, stronger governance and partner relationships, more efficient cash management with unfettered access to combined cash flows, better equity and debt market access, and employee retention, targeting US$1 billion revenue by FY28. No margin or valuation figures.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bac78e04-41ab-4077-b171-d4593bb411ad.pdf)* — Management said AI is not confined to the GBS reporting bucket but spread across the company — e.g. the SecAIGenie platform inside the security delivery and offerings — so restricting AI work to GBS would hurt growth. “So, AI has taken over many parts of, just to take an example, security.”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bac78e04-41ab-4077-b171-d4593bb411ad.pdf)* — The only carve-out described on the call is analytical: review the entire revenue stream project by project, classify by AI impact/relevance rather than technology, and disclose AI-led revenue as a share of the quarter's INR 625 crores. “So, if we are if we are INR625 crores this quarter, how many crores is led by AI?”
- *[Jul 2026](https://www.bseindia.com/stockinfo/AnnPdfOpen.aspx?Pname=bac78e04-41ab-4077-b171-d4593bb411ad.pdf)* — A timeline was given for that disclosure: the exercise finishes by end-September, with the number published at the end of Q2. “So that's the attempt that we have started, we have a plan that by end of September we will finish that exercise and give you in end of Q2.”
- *Scheme* — The transaction is an amalgamation, not a separation: Happiest Minds is absorbed into ITC Infotech India Limited and dissolved without winding up, under an MFA dated August 31, 2026 also signed by Mr Ashok Soota and Ashok Soota Medical Research LLP. “Post the Scheme becoming effective, the Transferor Company shall be dissolved without being wound up.”
- *Scheme* — First stated benefit is a single global platform built from complementary capabilities, customers and talent, yielding efficiency, governance and long-term value. “Creation of a single, globally credible platform by combining complementary capabilities, customer relationships and talent pools of the Companies, leading to greater operational efficiency, stronger governance and long -term value creation.”
- *Scheme* — Synergies are to come from pooling shared financial, managerial, technical and marketing resources into a unified technology platform and service offering. “Realisation of greater synergies between the businesses of the Transferor Company and Transferee Company and creation of a unified technology platform and service offering, through the use of shared financial, managerial, technical,”
- *Scheme* — Scale, cross-selling to a larger customer base, productivity, partner-ecosystem relationships and intellectual capital are cited as creating value for shareholders, customers, lenders and employees — the only place lenders are mentioned, as beneficiaries rather than requesters. “Increase in scale, focus, innovations in technology and expanded reach with increased growth opportunities, higher cross -selling opportunities to a larger base of customers, enhanced customer experience through integrated capabilities, improvement in produ ctivity and operational efficiencies, development of stronger relationships across the partner ecosystem, usage of augmented intellectual capital and stronger implementation capabilities resulting from the Amalgamation, thereby leading to value creation fo r the shareholders, customers, lenders, employees, etc.”
- *Scheme* — Cash-management efficiency and unrestricted access to the combined cash flows for funding growth is an explicit motive. “Achievement of greater efficiency in cash management of the combined entity, and unfettered access to cash flow generated from the combined businesses which can be deployed more efficiently to fund growth opportunities, in order to maximise shareholder’s v alue.”
- *Scheme* — Improving the Transferee's access to equity and debt capital markets is separately listed as a benefit. “Augmentation of the ability of the Transferee Company to raise capital from equity and debt markets to fund its growth requirements.”
- *Scheme* — Consideration ratio is 25 ITC Infotech shares of INR 10 for every 81 Happiest Minds shares of INR 2, with ITC Infotech shares to be listed by virtue of the scheme. “The Transferee Company shall issue and allot 25 fully paid -up equity shares of INR 10 (Indian Rupees Ten only) each of the Transferee Company for every 81 fully paid up equity shares of INR 2 (Indian Rupees Two only) each held by the shareholders of the Transferor Company  (other than Transferee Company itself) , as on the Record Date .”
- *Scheme* — The ratio rests on a joint valuation report of August 31, 2026 from PwC Business Consulting Services LLP and GT Valuation Advisors, with ICICI Securities providing the fairness opinion; the parties are not related parties. “The share exchange ratio  for the amalgamation is based on the valuation report dated August  31, 2026 , issued jointly by PwC Business Consulting Services LLP (Registration No. IBBI/RV -E/02/2022/158) and GT Valuation Advisors Private Limited (Registration No. IBBI/RV -E/05/2020/134), Registered Valuers .”
- *Scheme* — The press release sets the headline target and scale: US$1 billion revenue by FY28, 19,000+ employees, 800+ customers, 30+ countries, with ITC Infotech also acquiring an aggregate minority stake (figure truncated). “Happiest Minds Technologies announces merger with ITC Infotech to create a scaled, AI First Global Technology Services Enterprise  with US$ 1 billion Revenue by FY281”

*Not explained on the calls:* No call discusses the merger at all: no synergy quantification, margin, valuation or timeline detail, no party shown asking for it, and ITC Infotech's minority stake is truncated.

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The texts supplied do not contain any rationale — this must be stated plainly rather than filled in. The 'CALL PASSAGES' section arrived empty (no earnings-call excerpts at all), and the document labelled 'SCHEME RATIONALE' is not a scheme of arrangement or its rationale section: it is a one-page Regulation 30 intimation letter from IEX to BSE and NSE dated July 15, 2026, signed by Vineet Harlalka, CFO, Company Secretary & Compliance Officer. All that document establishes factually is the mechanism and scale of the separation: Indian Gas Exchange Limited (IGX), described as an associate company of Indian Energy Exchange Limited (IEX), filed a draft red herring prospectus dated July 14, 2026 with SEBI and BSE on July 14, 2026, for a proposed initial public offer of IGX equity shares. The offer is structured purely as an offer for sale of up to 16,710,000 equity shares by IEX — i.e. IEX monetising/diluting its own holding, with no fresh-issue component mentioned — and remains subject to receipt of applicable approvals, market conditions and other relevant considerations. The letter refers back to an earlier intimation dated December 03, 2025, indicating the transaction was first disclosed then, but the content of that intimation is not included here. No reason for the separation, no financial or operating metrics, no named requesting party (investors, lenders or partners), and no expected benefit to either IEX or IGX appears anywhere in the material provided. Any rationale beyond the above would have to come from memory or outside sources, which the instructions forbid.

**How it evolved:** Only two dated waypoints exist in the supplied text, both from filings rather than earnings calls: an initial intimation dated December 03, 2025, which the July letter says this disclosure is 'in furtherance of', and the DRHP filing dated July 14, 2026, intimated to the exchanges on July 15, 2026. Because the CALL PASSAGES section is empty, there is no call-by-call record of how the idea surfaced, how management framed it, or whether the structure (offer for sale of up to 16,710,000 shares by IEX) changed between December 2025 and July 2026. No call labels or call dates can be cited.

**What management expects from it:** Not stated anywhere in the supplied texts. No expectation is expressed for either entity — nothing on margins, capital allocation, value unlocking, valuation or management focus. The filing records only mechanics: IEX selling up to 16,710,000 shares of IGX, its associate company, through an offer for sale in IGX's proposed IPO, subject to approvals and market conditions.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The separation is being effected as an IPO of IGX, an associate company of IEX; the DRHP is dated July 14, 2026 and was filed with SEBI and BSE on that date, following an earlier intimation of December 03, 2025. No rationale is given in the document. “In furtherance of our intimation dated December 03, 2025, and in terms of Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, we wish to inform that the Indian Gas Exchange Limited ("IGX"), an associate company of the Indian Energy Exchange Limited ("IEX"), has filed a draft red herring prospectus dated July 14, 2026 ("DRHP"), with the Securities and Exchange Board of India and BSE Limited on July 14, 2026, in connection with the proposed initial public offer of equity shares of IGX ("Offer").”
- *Scheme* — The only quantitative detail disclosed is the size and structure of the transaction: a pure offer for sale by IEX of up to 16,710,000 IGX equity shares, with no fresh issue mentioned, and conditional on approvals and market conditions. “The Offer comprises of an offer for sale of up to 16,710,000 equity shares by IEX, and remains subject to receipt of applicable approvals, market conditions, and other relevant considerations.”
- *Scheme* — The document is an exchange intimation under Regulation 30 of the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015, signed by IEX's CFO, Company Secretary & Compliance Officer — a disclosure instrument, not a scheme rationale, which is why no commercial reasoning appears in it. “Subject: Intimation under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, ("SEBI Listing Regulations") Filling of DRHP of Indian Gas Exchange Limited”

*Not explained on the calls:* Nearly everything: no call passages were supplied and the 'rationale' is only a Reg-30 letter. Missing: reasons, metrics, who asked, IEX stake pre/post, expected benefits.

- *In their words:* “AIIL currently holds 20,32,50,000 equity shares of the ISARC agg. to 88.37% of the total issued and paid-up share capital of ISARC.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The materials supplied do not contain any separation, demerger, spin-off or scheme-of-arrangement rationale for Authum Investment & Infrastructure Ltd. (AIIL), so no management reasoning for separating a business can be reconstructed from them. The 'CALL PASSAGES' section is empty — no earnings call text of any year was provided — and the section labelled 'SCHEME RATIONALE' is in fact three unrelated Regulation 30 / LODR intimations signed by Company Secretary Dipyanti Jaiswar: (1) an 18 August 2026 intimation of a rights-issue subscription in subsidiary India SME Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd. (ISARC), where AIIL holds 20,32,50,000 shares (88.37%), ISARC had net worth of Rs. 353.29 crore and turnover of Rs. 17.42 crore as of 31 March 2026 (Rs. 21.21 crore FY2024-25, Rs. 2.47 crore FY2023-24), and AIIL agreed to take 40,65,00,000 shares in a 2-for-1 rights issue at Rs. 10 face value, paying 25% (Rs. 2.50/share, Rs. 101,62,50,000) as application money; (2) a 28 July 2026 intimation that NCLT Ahmedabad approved on 27 July 2026 the IBC resolution plan of the Inox Neo Energies Ltd. (INEL, lead member) and AIIL consortium for Wind World (India) Ltd., with AIIL's financial commitment approx. Rs. 350 crore; and (3) an 11 July 2026 intimation that NCLT rejected on 7 July 2026 the Vas Infrastructure Ltd. resolution plan in which AIIL was Successful Resolution Applicant. The only business-splitting element anywhere in these texts is internal to the Wind World acquisition, not to AIIL: the plan allocates WWIL's IPP and power-sale undertaking and its O&M business to INEL and/or its affiliates, while AIIL and/or its affiliates take certain identified real estate/assets — a carve-up of an acquisition target between consortium members, with no stated rationale, no margin, capital or valuation argument, and no party identified as having asked for it. These filings state the opposite of a separation in AIIL's own portfolio: AIIL is adding capital to ISARC and acquiring assets, and the Vas rejection is stated to have 'no impact on the business operations of the Company.' Answering the question as asked would require inventing management commentary that is not in the supplied material, which I will not do.

**How it evolved:** No evolution can be traced: there are no tagged earnings calls and no dated management commentary on a separation. The only chronology available from the filings is of acquisitions and insolvency outcomes — 2 April 2025 (AIIL emerges as Successful Resolution Applicant for Vas Infrastructure), 17 June 2025 (AIIL acquires majority of ISARC), 20 February 2026 (Wind World consortium announcement), 7 July 2026 (NCLT rejects the Vas plan), 27 July 2026 (NCLT approves the Wind World plan), 18 August 2026 (ISARC rights-issue subscription). Nothing in this sequence is presented by the company as leading toward, or arising from, a separation of a business.

**What management expects from it:** Not stated. The texts contain no management expectation for a separation — no commentary on margins, capital allocation, valuation re-rating or management focus for any resulting entity. The only forward-looking statements are that AIIL will make further rights-issue call payments to ISARC and update the exchanges, and that the Vas rejection leaves operations unaffected.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — Within the Wind World (India) Ltd. insolvency acquisition, the consortium plan splits WWIL's businesses between members — INEL and/or affiliates take the IPP/power-sale undertaking and the O&M business, AIIL and/or affiliates take identified real estate/assets. This is the only separation of any business described in the supplied texts, and the filing gives no reason for the split. “The Resolution Plan submitted by the consortium of INEL and the Company inter alia envisaged that INEL as the Lead Member and/or its affiliates shall acquire (i) the IPP and power sale undertaking; and (ii) the operations and maintenance (O&M) business of WWIL, while the Company and/or its affiliates shall acquire certain identified real estate / assets from WWIL.”
- *Scheme* — The 18 August 2026 filing is a capital infusion into a subsidiary, not a separation: AIIL subscribes to a 2:1 rights issue in ISARC (88.37%-held) purely to fund the subsidiary's general business requirements, paying Rs. 101.625 crore as 25% application money on 40,65,00,000 shares. “Currently, Authum Investment & Infrastructure Limited is holding 88.37% share capital of ISARC and on account of Rights Issues offered by ISARC, the Company has accepted to invest further serving the subsidiary to meet its capital requirement for general business operations.”
- *Scheme* — The 11 July 2026 filing records NCLT's 7 July 2026 rejection of the Vas Infrastructure resolution plan in which AIIL was the Successful Resolution Applicant, and expressly states the rejection does not affect AIIL's operations — again no mention of separating any business. “We would further like to state that on account of the aforesaid rejection of the resolution plan there is no impact on the business operations of the Company.”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything: no earnings call passages were supplied, no scheme rationale, no demerged undertaking, ratio, record date, appointed date, listing plan, or any reason, requester or benefit for a separation.

**What is being separated, as the documents put it:** Nothing is spun off; this is an amalgamation of Cigniti Technologies Limited into Coforge Limited — class `regulatory_strategic`.

- *Insiders:* not stated
- *What it reveals:* Acquired business's EBITDA margin expanded from ~11% to ~19% in five-six quarters; top two accounts scaled from $25m to $75m annually; reported PAT at 14-15%; new US$2.5bn firm with US$2bn AI-led Engineering, Data and Cloud core.
- *Selling pressure:* unclear — Documents do not discuss share-flow; Cigniti minority holders receive 1 Coforge share per Cigniti share held
- *Parent or spin:* parent · *option pricing date:* not stated
- *Read next:* Income Tax Department's reported outstanding demand of Rs 3,04,77,45,392 against Coforge, and Annexure P-14 litigation details
- *In their words:* “Coforge acquired Cigniti to gain access to its tenured relationships, expand its Healthcare business, and grow its presence in the Midwest and Western regions of the US.”

### Why the demerger — three years of calls and the scheme

The texts provided do not describe a separation, spin-off or demerger at all, and no earnings-call passages were supplied — the CALL PASSAGES section is empty, so nothing can be attributed to management commentary. What the filing text describes is the opposite transaction: a Scheme of Amalgamation in which Cigniti Technologies Limited (the Transferor Company, a digital assurance and engineering / software-testing business using AI-driven Continuous Testing and Test Automation, listed on BSE and NSE) is merged into Coforge Limited (the Transferee Company, an IT and IT-enabled services provider across financial services, insurance, travel, transportation and logistics, manufacturing and distribution, and government). The commercial backdrop given is that Coforge had already bought control before the scheme: by 27 December 2024 it held 54% of Cigniti's expanded share capital, having acquired 72,35,865 equity shares between October and December 2024 for approximately INR 10,239 million, and both boards approved the original scheme that same day, 27 December 2024. Consideration was set by a Joint Valuation Report of PwC Business Consulting Services LLP and KPMG Valuation Services LLP at a share exchange ratio of 1:5 (one INR 10 Coforge share for five INR 10 Cigniti shares), with fairness opinions from JM Financial Limited and Axis Capital Limited. That ratio was later restated to 1:1 by a Joint Clarification Note dated 13 June 2025 purely because Coforge split each INR 10 share into five INR 2 shares (board 04 March 2025, shareholders 17 April 2025, record date 04 June 2025); the filing stresses the revised ratio is "mathematically and economically equivalent" to the original and conveys no substantive change in value, with Axis (16 June 2025) and JM Financial (19 June 2025) reconfirming fairness, and both boards approving the amended scheme on 06 July 2025. Critically, the extract itself does not reproduce the rationale: it states the rationale "ha[s] been set out in detail in the First Motion Order dated 17 October 2025" and is only "briefly recapitulated herein", and the recapitulation that follows is procedural — incorporation history, registered-office shifts to Gurugram, share capital, exchange ratio, exchange and tribunal steps — with no stated synergy, margin, capital, focus or valuation reasoning. No investor, lender or partner is identified as having asked for the transaction; stakeholders simply voted in favour, and no objections were received from any shareholder or creditor.

**How it evolved:** No earnings calls were provided, so there is no call-by-call evolution and no call dates to cite. The only sequence available is from the filing: board approval of the original scheme plus the 1:5 valuation and fairness opinions on 27 December 2024, after Coforge's October–December 2024 purchase of 54% of Cigniti; the Coforge stock split (board 04 March 2025, shareholders 17 April 2025, record date 04 June 2025) prompting the 13 June 2025 restatement of the ratio to 1:1 and amended board approvals on 06 July 2025; then NSE and BSE observation letters on 17 and 18 July 2025, the First Motion Order of 17 October 2025, stakeholder meetings on 06 December 2025, Chairperson's Reports of 08 December 2025, the Second Motion petition filed 15 December 2025, and admission by the Tribunal on 09 January 2026. That is a change in transaction mechanics and process, not a change in a separation plan.

**What management expects from it:** Nothing is stated. The supplied texts contain no management expectations for margins, capital allocation, valuation or business focus, and no post-transaction operating or financial targets for either entity. The filing's substantive assertions are limited to consideration being fair (1:1 post-split, economically identical to 1:5) and procedural compliance; benefits are said to be detailed only in the First Motion Order, which is not included.

**Point by point, with the source:**

- *Scheme* — The transaction is an amalgamation of Cigniti Technologies into Coforge, not a separation of any business. “In The Matter Of Scheme Of Amalgamation Between Cigniti Technologies Limited And Coforge Limited”
- *Scheme* — The filing extract does not actually contain the rationale; it defers to the First Motion Order and only summarises formalities. “The main objects, dates of incorporation, authorised and paid-up share capital, and the rationale of the Scheme have been set out in detail in the First Motion Order dated 17 October 2025, and are briefly recapitulated herein.”
- *Scheme* — Coforge had already acquired majority control of Cigniti for about INR 10,239 million before the scheme was approved, on the same date as board approval. “It is pertinent to note that as on 27 December 2024, the Transferee Company already held 54% of the expanded share capital of the Transferor Company, having acquired 72,35,865 equity shares between October and December 2024 for approximately INR 10,239 million.”
- *Scheme* — Cigniti's described business is AI-led software testing / digital assurance, distinct from Coforge's vertical-led IT services business. “The Transferor Company is engaged in providing digital assurance and engineering (software testing) services globally, leveraging AI-driven Continuous Testing and Test Automation solutions, and its equity shares are listed on BSE Limited ("BSE") and the National Stock Exchange of India Limited ("NSE").”
- *Scheme* — The ratio moved from 1:5 to 1:1 only because of Coforge's INR 10 to INR 2 stock split, with no change in economic value to Cigniti holders. “This revised 1:1 ratio is mathematically and economically equivalent to the original 1:5 ratio, the change being purely reflective of the post-split capital structure of the Transferee Company and not representing any substantive change in the economic value accruing to the shareholders of the Transferor Company.”
- *Scheme* — Valuation and fairness were supported by two registered valuers and two merchant bankers at the 1:5 stage. “a Joint Valuation Report was issued by Registered Valuers, PwC Business Consulting Services LLP and KPMG Valuation Services LLP, recommending a Share Exchange Ratio of 1:5”
- *Scheme* — Lenders and shareholders of both companies supported the scheme unanimously or near-unanimously; Coforge's secured creditors voting ₹3,82,07,27,619 in value were all in favour, and Cigniti had no secured creditors. “It is submitted that no objections whatsoever were received from any stakeholder in relation to the Scheme.”
- *Scheme* — Competition clearance was not needed, the combination being exempt. “Notification of the Scheme to the Competition Commission of India is not required, the same being exempted under Schedule I of the CCI (Procedure in regard to the Transaction of Business relating to Combination) Regulations, 2011”

*Not explained on the calls:* Everything substantive: no earnings-call passages were supplied, and the extract omits the actual rationale — no synergy, margin, capital, focus, valuation or stakeholder-demand reasoning, and no separation.
